result.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
result.summary: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort. We address this limitation by deriving five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces from complementary offline assessments. Based on this characterization, we propose SWEAR, a difficulty-aware reasoning framework that learns difficulty signals during supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adapt reasoning allocation across reasoning stages. Experiments on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR show that SWEAR improves accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens, shortening reasoning for easy instances without sacrificing performance on difficult ones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对大音频语言模型自适应推理中难度估计过于粗糙的问题，提出 SWEAR：由离线评估导出五维难度分数与压缩推理轨迹，在 SFT 阶段学习难度信号，再用强化学习在不同推理阶段分配推理量，在 MMAU-test-mini 与 MMAR 上提升准确率并明显减少生成 token。
AI.relevance_reason: 模态是音频而非视觉，但「难度信号驱动的推理量分配」可能为 LVR 的动态计算与停止决策提供可核查线索，例如五维难度与压缩轨迹如何对应 latent 推理状态所需的深度与内容。
